title: Autoscale signal racing caused transient underprovisioning; root cause and safe restart playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: During a sustained burst test on 2025-02-14 we observed intermittent 5xx errors and elevated tail latency for the inference frontends. Root cause analysis shows multiple autoscaler signals raced and caused repeated transient underscale cycles that produced cold-start cascades. This ticket captures the investigation, immediate mitigations, and a documented safe restart/playbook to prevent operator actions from worsening autoscaler instability.
impact_summary: ~2 hours of elevated 500/502 responses across two customer namespaces in eu-west-1 (approx 03:12–05:26 UTC). Peak request loss ~2.4% of requests; median latency unaffected but p95/p99 spiked due to cold starts. No data loss. Affected customers reported degraded availability for latency-sensitive flows.
timeline:
2025-02-14 03:05 UTC: Synthetic load generator ramped to 2.5x baseline.
2025-02-14 03:12 UTC: First spike in 5xx observed; HPA and KEDA triggered multiple rapid scaling events.
2025-02-14 03:20 UTC: Control-plane traces show KEDA scaler webhook reported multiple trigger deltas; HPA reconciliations overlapped with cooldown windows.
2025-02-14 03:30–04:10 UTC: Repeated oscillation: scale up -> short-lived traffic -> scale down -> cold starts -> errors.
2025-02-14 04:15 UTC: On-call initiated manual stabilization: increase minReplicas, pin target CPU and queue-length thresholds, temporarily disable aggressive KEDA scaler.
2025-02-14 05:26 UTC: Traffic stabilized after conservative autoscaler parameters applied and a short warm pool pre-warming job executed.
2025-02-14 06:00 UTC: Post-incident data collection and tracing completed; working group formed for RCA.
root_cause: Failure mode is multi-factor: (1) recent change in our request-probe sampling reduced smoothing from 60s to 10s for faster detection — this increased sensitivity and amplified short-lived bursts; (2) a bug in percentile aggregation for the queue-length metric caused spikes to appear higher than they were when aggregated across pods; (3) KEDA's scaler cooldown interacted poorly with HPA stabilization windows, leading to two controllers making conflicting decisions (racing scale up/down) and triggering repeated pod churn; (4) lack of an active warm-pool for this workload meant scale-downs produced cold-start latency that pushed p99 past SLOs.
steps_taken: Immediate mitigations during incident: (1) Raised minReplicas from 2 to 6 for affected services to provide buffer capacity. (2) Temporarily increased HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds to 90s and KEDA cooldown to 120s to prevent flip-flopping. (3) Rolled back the probe sampling change to 60s on the traffic-facing cluster. (4) Launched small warm-pool job to pre-initialize model artifacts on new nodes. (5) Engaged customer success for impacted accounts and posted an incident banner.
long_term_mitigations: Planned mitigations: (1) Implement autoscaler arbiter service that serializes scaling decisions from KEDA/HPA and enforces a global cooldown policy. (2) Fix percentile aggregation bug in metrics pipeline and backfill tests for cross-pod percentile correctness. (3) Provide workload-specific warm-pool templates and autopilot warm-pool rules for latency-sensitive models. (4) Add canary and staging gating for any probe-sensitivity tuning and require perf bench sign-off. (5) Add automated detection that alerts when the ratio of scale-downs to scale-ups exceeds threshold within a window.

postmortem_notes: Key learning: making detection faster (probe sensitivity) without end-to-end consideration of controller interactions introduces systemic risk. Autoscaling behavior must be evaluated as a distributed control problem, not isolated component updates. Operational playbooks must make it explicit which knobs to change (minReplicas, stabilizationWindowSeconds, KEDA cooldown, warm-pool toggles) and the order to apply them to avoid worsening oscillations.
